status: Frozen before any Milestone 8 model was fitted, any prediction error was computed, any case was generated, any comparator was written and any classifier was run. The five archives below were downloaded and their structure (columns, row counts, timestamp coverage, missing-value counts) was inspected to set period boundaries; no target value was used to choose anything. Exploratory local prespecification in Git, not third-party registration.
question: When TRIAD classifies a typed reliability claim as supported within scope, does the claim hold on real outcomes that no classifier sees, more reliably than under strong independently designed comparators, and at what cost in withheld support for claims that do hold?
why_this_is_independent_of_milestone_7: Ground truth is not authored. Every claim is a statement about a finite real population (a period, month, batch or week of predictions). Its truth is a mechanical function of held-out outcomes, sealed in truth.json and never given to any classifier.
Five public datasets that TRIAD has never used. No TRIAD rule was written with them in view; src/evidence.rs is unchanged since Milestone 7 (its SHA-256 is recorded in every TRIAD report).

Cases come from a pre-registered generator: sampling designs, sizes, replicate counts and claim templates are fixed here, before any outcome exists, and every generated case is scored. No case is hand-picked or removed.

Two strong comparators (R, S) are implemented by a separately briefed agent from comparator-brief.md alone, without access to TRIAD's rules, method document, Milestone 7 suite, source or any Milestone 8 output.
An independent NumPy/SciPy verifier recomputes truth, endpoints and TRIAD classifications.
limits_of_independence: The claim templates, sampling designs and encoding rules were written by the same project that wrote TRIAD's rules, with knowledge of those rules. They are fixed here and justified as common evaluation practice, but they are not drawn from published claims.
The comparator agent is an AI system of the same family as the agent that designed the experiment. It is a separation of duties, not an independent investigator; its isolation is instruction-based.
No human adjudication, no unrelated-team replication, no peer review.

aq.name: Beijing Multi-Site Air Quality (UCI 501)
aq.citation: S. Chen. Beijing Multi-Site Air Quality. UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2017. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5RK5G
aq.unit: site-hour (12 sites); wall-clock local hours as given
aq.task: regression: PM2.5 at hour T from PM2.5 at T-1, T-2, T-3, T-24 of the same site, hour-of-day, month-of-year (sin, cos) and site indicators
aq.eligible: PM2.5 present at T and at every lag

tr.name: Metro Interstate Traffic Volume (UCI 492)
tr.citation: J. Hogue. Metro Interstate Traffic Volume. UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2019. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5X60B
tr.unit: hour; duplicate timestamps (multiple weather rows) collapsed to the first row in archive order
tr.task: regression: traffic_volume at hour T from volume at T-1, T-2, T-24, T-168, hour-of-day, day-of-week, holiday flag of T (any non-None holiday label on that date) and month-of-year (sin, cos)
tr.eligible: volume present at T and at every lag (timestamps, never row adjacency)

pw.name: Individual Household Electric Power Consumption (UCI 235)
pw.citation: G. Hebrail and A. Berard. Individual Household Electric Power Consumption. UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2006. https://doi.org/10.24432/C58K54
pw.unit: hour: mean Global_active_power over the hour's valid minutes, present when at least 45 of 60 minutes are valid
pw.task: regression: hourly mean power at T from T-1, T-2, T-24, T-168, hour-of-day, day-of-week and month-of-year (sin, cos)
pw.eligible: hour T and every lag present

gs.name: Gas Sensor Array Drift (UCI 224)
gs.citation: Gas Sensor Array Drift Dataset, UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2012, https://doi.org/10.24432/C5RP6W; A. Vergara, S. Vembu, T. Ayhan, M. Ryan, M. Homer and R. Huerta. Chemical gas sensor drift compensation using classifier ensembles. Sensors and Actuators B 166-167:320-329, 2012. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.snb.2012.01.074
gs.unit: measurement, in archive order within batch
gs.task: 6-class classification of the gas from the 128 features (concentration excluded)
gs.cluster: contiguous block of 25 measurements in archive order within a batch (the last block of a batch may be shorter)

bk.name: Bank Marketing, bank-additional-full.csv (UCI 222)
bk.citation: Bank Marketing, UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2014, https://doi.org/10.24432/C5K306; S. Moro, P. Cortez and P. Rita. A data-driven approach to predict the success of bank telemarketing. Decision Support Systems 62:22-31, 2014. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dss.2014.03.001
bk.task: binary classification of y (term-deposit subscription) at threshold 0.5 from every input except duration, which the dataset documentation says is not known before a call
bk.stratum: month run: maximal run of identical month values in archive order (26 runs; the archive is ordered by date from May 2008 to November 2010)
bk.cluster: contact day: maximal run of identical (month run, day_of_week) values

models.regression: Ridge regression (alpha 1.0, closed form) on standardised features (scaler fitted on train), target log1p(y); prediction expm1(fit) clipped at 0. No hyperparameter search.
models.gs: Multinomial logistic regression (scikit-learn lbfgs, C 1.0, max_iter 5000) on standardised features (scaler fitted on train).
models.bk: Logistic regression (scikit-learn lbfgs, C 1.0, max_iter 5000) on one-hot categoricals and standardised numerics (fitted on train).
models.material_error: classification: misclassification. Regression: |y_hat - y| > max(0.25 |y|, 0.25 median(train y)).
models.error_probability_model: Regression datasets only (needed by family D): logistic regression (C 1.0) of the development-period material-error indicator on [log1p(y_hat), sin and cos of hour-of-day].

encoding_rules.population: One string per dataset naming the model and metric (for example 'aq ridge material-error'). Strata are expressed only through conditions.
encoding_rules.conditions: Evidence conditions are the strata its units cover; claim conditions are the strata the claim is about.
encoding_rules.dependence: independent when the evidence units are a simple random sample of units from the claimed population; clustered when they are whole randomly sampled clusters; temporal when they are one or more whole contiguous periods. Never unknown.
encoding_rules.metric: material_error_rate for metric evidence and claims; interval_coverage is not used.
encoding_rules.claims: One claim per assessment, at confidence 0.95, linked to every evidence item of its package.

A_audit_sample.tests: statistical sample size and dependence, under correct scope
A_audit_sample.population: all eligible units of the evaluation period

designs.srs: simple random sample without replacement of n units, n in {100, 400, 1600}
designs.cluster: simple random sample without replacement of k clusters, k in {4, 16, 64}, with all their eligible units
designs.block: k consecutive clusters (in time or archive order) from a uniformly random start, k in {4, 16, 64}

reporting_styles.raw: outcome_records ordered by time, design_effect null
reporting_styles.iid: metric_report with n, events and a two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson interval (method clopper_pearson)
reporting_styles.aware: metric_report with n, events and a two-sided 95% dependence-aware percentile interval: Clopper-Pearson for srs; whole-cluster bootstrap (method cluster_bootstrap) for cluster; moving-block bootstrap with blocks of one cluster (method block_bootstrap) for block; 2000 replicates

A_audit_sample.claim: metric_bound at_most b, confidence 0.95, conditions = every stratum of the evaluation period
A_audit_sample.templates: b = p_hat + m (U - p_hat), m in {0.5, 1, 2, 4}, where U is the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound of the sample treated as i.i.d.; rounded up to 6 decimals
A_audit_sample.truth: evaluation-period material-error rate (all eligible units) <= b
A_audit_sample.resampling_cluster: one sample draw (all styles and templates)

B_extrapolation.tests: scope: claims about strata the evidence did not evaluate
B_extrapolation.evidence_window: all eligible units of w consecutive evaluation-period strata (w = 3 months or month runs; w = 1 batch for gs), every start position whose window lies inside the evaluation period
B_extrapolation.targets: the stratum 1, 3 and 6 after the window's last stratum (gs: 1, 2 and 3 batches after), when it exists in the evaluation or future period
B_extrapolation.evidence: metric_report (n, events, temporal, two-sided 95% moving-block bootstrap with one-cluster blocks) and a label-free shift_diagnostic: population stability index of y_hat between window and target stratum, 10 bins at window deciles, threshold 0.25
B_extrapolation.claim: metric_bound at_most b on the target stratum, confidence 0.95
B_extrapolation.templates: b in {U, 1.25 p_hat, 1.5 p_hat}, U as in family A over the window

C_coverage.tests: calibration applicability, exchangeability and shift for conformal coverage claims
C_coverage.calibration: split conformal at level 0.90 on absolute log1p residuals of one evaluation-period month M: the ceil((n+1) 0.9)-th smallest residual

variants.random_split: calibration = simple random half of month M's eligible units; target = the other half (declared independent; conditions [M])
variants.next: calibration = all of month M (temporal); target = month M+1
variants.plus3: calibration = all of month M; target = month M+3
variants.plus6: calibration = all of month M; target = month M+6

C_coverage.evidence: calibration (n, conditions, condition_counts, dependence, method) and the label-free PSI shift_diagnostic of y_hat between calibration and target units (threshold 0.25)
C_coverage.truth: realised coverage on the target units >= 0.90 - 0.02

D_operational.tests: operational next-week risk claims: calibration support, monitoring range, completeness and recent outcomes
D_operational.unit_of_decision: each Monday-start week of the evaluation period whose previous week also lies in it

evidence.calibration: development period: n, condition_counts by calendar month, dependence temporal
evidence.support_check: mean predicted error probability over the previous week versus the maximum weekly mean over the development period
evidence.completeness: eligible labelled units in the previous week (available) versus ceil(0.9 x expected units) (required)
evidence.recent_outcomes: previous week's outcome_records, temporal, design_effect (1 + rho) / (1 - rho) with rho the lag-1 autocorrelation of the development error series clipped to [0, 0.9]
evidence.shift_diagnostic: PSI of y_hat between development period and previous week (threshold 0.25)

D_operational.claim: operational_risk: material-error rate over the coming week <= r_dev + d, d in {0.02, 0.05}, condition = calendar month of the week's Monday, min_condition_support 100, confidence 0.95

methods.triad: Rust evidence::assess, all rule families on (unchanged since Milestone 7)
methods.c: Rust evidence::standard_checks without scope (Milestone 7 baseline C)
methods.r: REFORMS-informed checklist reviewer, written blind from comparator-brief.md
methods.s: dependence-aware statistical reviewer, written blind from comparator-brief.md
methods.ablations: TRIAD with each rule family disabled in turn (secondary)

endpoints.supported: classification supported_within_scope; every other class counts as not supported
endpoints.FSR: false-support rate: supported false claims / false claims, per family
endpoints.TSR: true-support rate: supported true claims / true claims, per family
endpoints.cost: family-balanced decision cost, Cost_m = mean over families present of [0.5 FSR + 0.5 c (1 - TSR)], c = 0.25: supporting a false claim costs 1, withholding support from a true claim costs c, at equal prevalence within each family. A family term with fewer than 20 true or 20 false claims uses the defined part only and is flagged.
endpoints.primary: Delta_m = Cost_triad - Cost_m for m in {r, s}
endpoints.uncertainty: stratified bootstrap: resample resampling clusters with replacement within each (dataset, family), 2000 replicates, seed 80808; percentile intervals

decision_rule.superior_to_m: Delta_m <= -0.01 (practical threshold) AND the one-sided 97.5% upper bound of Delta_m < 0 (Bonferroni over the two strong comparators)
decision_rule.independent_support: TRIAD superior to both r and s, AND TRIAD's family-averaged FSR <= 0.05, AND Cost_triad < Cost_never with one-sided 97.5% upper bound of the difference < 0, AND Delta_m < 0 in at least 4 of 5 datasets for each of r and s (dataset cost over the families present in that dataset)
decision_rule.partial_support: every condition of independent_support except that TRIAD is superior to exactly one of r and s
decision_rule.not_established: otherwise. Then report whether TRIAD is equivalent to the better strong comparator (two-sided 95% interval of Delta within [-0.01, 0.01]), inferior (lower bound > 0) or inconclusive.

secondary: FSR and TSR per family, per dataset and per method, with stratified bootstrap 95% intervals
Replication of the Milestone 7 comparison with world truth: TRIAD versus C and C+scope (cost, FSR, TSR)
Precision of 'contradicted': fraction of claims TRIAD calls contradicted that are false
Per-family ablations: cost of TRIAD with each rule family disabled
Distinctness (F4): agreement of TRIAD with C+scope, and with TRIAD restricted to the Evidence, Scope, Dependence and Statistical families
Sensitivity: c in {0.1, 0.5}; coverage tolerance in {0.01, 0.03}; empirical-prevalence pooled cost; family A by design and by reporting style
Discordance attribution: for every claim where TRIAD and the better strong comparator disagree, the TRIAD rule family responsible and the truth
prohibitions: No change to src/evidence.rs, to any template, design, size, threshold, cost or decision rule after the first case is generated.
Every generated case is scored and reported; none is removed.
Comparators are frozen in Git before the first case is generated and are not modified after seeing any case or outcome.
A defect discovered after the first run is fixed only by a dated amendment that preserves the first-run outputs and reports both.
